faq.q: What are the URL-safe and padding checkboxes for?
faq.a: URL-safe Base64 swaps + and / for - and _ so the string is safe in URLs and filenames. The padding checkbox controls whether trailing = characters are kept. Encoding is UTF-8 aware (via TextEncoder), so accented characters and emoji round-trip correctly rather than corrupting, which plain btoa would do. When decoding, it auto-fixes missing padding and detects URL-safe input.

faq.q: Can I turn a file into Base64, and get a ready-to-use CSS snippet?
faq.a: Yes. Drop one or more files on the File tab. For an image you get a size readout with the percentage overhead, a live preview, and a copy-ready background-image: url("data:...") CSS snippet. You can output either raw Base64 or the full data URI including the MIME type. Files over about 8MB trigger a slow-encoding warning.

faq.q: How does Base64 → File detect the file type?
faq.a: Paste a data URI and it reads the MIME type directly; paste raw Base64 and it inspects the first bytes (magic numbers) to identify PNG, JPEG, GIF, PDF, ZIP, WAV, MP3, BMP or XML, falling back to octet-stream. It then downloads with a matching extension, or a filename you supply. Images are also previewed before download.

faq.q: What do the Hex and URL tabs add?
faq.a: The Hex tab converts text to space-separated hex bytes and back (UTF-8), rejecting odd-length or non-hex input. The URL tab offers Encode (encodeURI), Encode Component (encodeURIComponent) and Decode, treating + as a space on decode. Your text draft, chosen options and active tab are autosaved in your browser and restored on reload; a Clear draft button removes them.
